title: Screen generated-lattice parity cuts before mixed-target word search
body:
## Summary

```text
8 rank-one paid frames, 3 invertible unequal-class targets
  rational rank cuts: pass all 220 paid spans
  determinant equality: pass
  generated-lattice parity cut: 1 paid call < 3 target roles, reject
```

Adds one package, `research/bit-generated-lattice-parity-cuts/`, with a written necessary-cut proof, exact separating example and reusable bounded CLI. Every character of the actual generated lattice H/2H is checked. The rejection holds for every call order and any finite number of restored dirty scalar roles.

This takes the unequal-class pre-search handoff from #2900/#2934. It does not exclude every unequal-class candidate or construct a supplier. The augmentation equation and determinant condition are inherited; the new result is the complete character-cut checker and separation from rational cuts plus determinant equality.

Scientific base `d3add2cc28e958bedec197ab32b5526c5a222628`, priority revision 5. Refreshed main `991c50d1ea8ddb7cf88c1b4a45c7b409c02d38fb` changes no guidance, selected record or pinned mathematical input. Exact pins and overlap coverage are in TASK.json/SOURCES.json. [Canonical claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2898#discussioncomment-18973523).

Credit Tuafo's augmentation argument, Ali Romman's PR468 projection/register method, the retained eumemic/PR288 and huxint/PR203 lineage, mixed-target compression and the rational-cut screen. Pending #2934 is pinned as context only, not used as a theorem. Predecessor files stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the retained rational-cut CLI accepts the exact example across all 220 paid spans; its target determinants are 400, 256 and 152 and determinant equality holds.
- **After:** the character `X11 modulo 2` retains one paid frame and all three targets. A rank-one projector cannot equal the resulting rank-three matrix. All 64 generated-lattice characters are checked; minimum margin is -2.
- Every six-frame subset is independent, proving all rational cuts pass. The three target classes are distinct, so the example is outside #2934's equal-class hypothesis.
- 5,676 independent Cramer/gcd/primitive-relation oracle cases, six behavioral groups, three semantic implementation mutants and receipt corruptions pass. Maximum-rank coverage checks all 4,096 characters.
- Registered CPython 3.12.15 replay, optimized CPython 3.13.5 replay, all 144 research-workflow tests without skips, Ruff, warning-as-error compilation and committed-byte preflight pass locally on Linux/WSL2. Hosted CI is separate.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-generated-lattice-parity-cuts
python3 -I -O -B research/bit-generated-lattice-parity-cuts/verify.py
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
```

The written proof establishes the universal necessary inequality; the finite checks corroborate its implementation. No independent human or proof-kernel review, full predecessor/selected cold replay, native realization, hosting, precision/tape or complete supplier moment is claimed. No new kappa. A passing screen remains only necessary.

## Merge danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast radius:** research.

One new opt-in package. No selected frontier, supplier, frozen input, shared runner or existing verifier changes.
